chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) told me, from his paternal uncle, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Husayn ibn Ayub ibn Abi Aqeela al-Sayrafi, from Ikram al-Khath'ami, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Beware of rulership, and beware of stepping on the heel bones of men. So I said: May I be sacrificed for you, as for rulership, I have known it, and as for me to step on the heel bones of men, then two thirds of what is in my hands is from nothing but what has stepped on the heel bones of men. So he said: It is not as you think. Beware from assigning a man (as a leader), besides the Proof, by which you believe him in everything he says.

key_terms.أَعْقَابَ الرِّجَالِ: Heel bones of men (metaphor for authority/subjugation)
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The Proof (referring to the Imam or the ultimate authority)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'stepping on the heel bones of men' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against *al-Ri'asah* (leadership/authority) by cautioning against elevating a specific leader to the status of the ultimate Proof (al-Hujjah) and accepting his infallibility in all matters. The metaphor of 'stepping on the heel bones' signifies the humility required when exercising authority, ensuring one does not become arrogant or treat subordinates as inferior. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of *Tawqif* (divine designation) versus *Ijtihad* (scholarly deduction), distinguishing between the infallible Imam and fallible leaders or scholars.
